question: A 7-year-old boy is brought with chronic mouth breathing, snoring, and recurrent ear infections. Examination reveals an open-mouthed appearance, elongated face, high-arched palate, and crowded upper teeth. Which condition best explains this constellation?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Allergic rhinitis can cause nasal obstruction and mouth breathing, but it would not typically produce the dentoskeletal changes (elongated face, high-arched palate, crowded teeth) seen here, which result from chronic obligate mouth breathing due to nasopharyngeal obstruction.

Correct. The described features — adenoid facies — result from chronic nasopharyngeal obstruction by hypertrophied adenoids. Long-standing mouth breathing prevents the normal mechanical shaping of the palate by the tongue, leading to high-arched palate and dental malocclusion.

Incorrect. DNS typically causes unilateral nasal obstruction in adults; it is not the primary cause of chronic bilateral nasal obstruction in a young child, and it does not explain the recurrent ear infections or the classic facies described.
Incorrect. Bilateral choanal atresia presents at birth with cyclical cyanosis (relieved by crying) and is an immediate neonatal emergency; it would not present as a chronic condition in a 7-year-old.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the clinical presentation section. Adenoid hypertrophy in children causes a distinctive pattern of features beyond simple nasal blockage.
Correct. Adenoid facies is a recognisable constellation resulting from long-standing nasopharyngeal obstruction in childhood.
